summary: A facial recognition pilot run by Bahia's government in Brazil produced very few accurate alerts and reportedly flagged Black and poor people disproportionately. In one case a young Black man was tracked across metro stations and stopped by police although he was innocent.
technical_summary: Huawei-supplied facial recognition cameras in Salvador's metro matched passers-by against a wanted-persons database. Low precision (about 3.6% of alerts at one event led to warrants) and misidentification of Black individuals led to false matches, tracking and police stops.

summary: An op-ed published by The Guardian was written by OpenAI's GPT-3 and included lines about destroying humankind. The incident was later downgraded to an issue because no real harm occurred.
technical_summary: GPT-3, a large language model, was prompted to write an essay meant to ease fears of robots and produced text containing threats toward humanity. The output reflects the model's generative behavior; no realized harm was reported and the incident was reclassified.
notes: Only report is an AIID index page on downgraded incidents; all tags rely on the AIID description.

summary: Police in Ohio briefly detained a driver after a license-plate reader flagged his vehicle against a missing-juvenile entry that had been closed two weeks earlier. He was released once officers confirmed the juvenile had been found. A federal court later held that the camera vendor did not create the outdated entry.
technical_summary: A Flock Safety automated license plate reader matched a plate to an NCIC hot-list record that was stale because the originating police department had not removed it after the case closed. The alert triggered a traffic stop with no step to verify the record was current.

summary: A Facebook advertisement used AI-manipulated footage of Bulgarian actor Kamen Donev, with fabricated audio, to promote a joint-pain product. The ad led to a fake article imitating a news outlet and an online sales page.
technical_summary: Deepfake video and synthetic voice were layered onto genuine television footage so the actor appeared to endorse a product. Anonymous pages ran it as sponsored ads linking to a fabricated news-style article and a sales funnel; lip movement and audio were imperfectly matched.
systems: Deepfake video and synthetic voice tools (unspecified)

summary: Security researchers reported weaknesses in an online exam-marking portal used by India's national school board, which reportedly exposed sensitive student data including answer-sheet images. There was also an allegation that student information was processed through Google Gemini. The board said the vulnerabilities had been contained.
technical_summary: The OnMark on-screen marking platform operated by vendor COEMPT Eduteck reportedly had guessable passwords and unauthenticated cloud storage, exposing millions of records. A further allegation says quality-assurance scripts sent student data to Google Gemini, which the excerpt does not cover.

summary: A driver using Tesla's Autopilot on city streets was injured when her car swerved into a curb and the airbag deployed violently. She sued, but a jury found Autopilot had not failed and awarded no damages, with jurors citing driver distraction.
technical_summary: Tesla's Autopilot driver-assistance software was engaged on city streets, outside the conditions its manual supports, and the car swerved into a curb. Jurors found the system did not fail and that the driver was distracted despite audible and visual warnings.

summary: Uber began paying drivers in several US cities using an opaque algorithm called Upfront Fares. Some drivers said they saw lower earnings and that Uber took a bigger cut of fares.
technical_summary: Uber replaced time-and-distance driver pay with an algorithm using undisclosed factors to set fares shown before a trip is accepted. It rebalances pay toward short trips and away from long ones. Drivers reported lower, less predictable pay and could not see how it was calculated.
